subtitle: What's confirmed and what isn't, with sources
stand: One laboratory technician at the Irkutsk Anti-Plague Institute, 28, died in a hospital in Shelekhov, Siberia, in the night of 1–2 October, two days after being admitted with severe pneumonia. Russian media and Telegram channels say it was pneumonic plague; Russia's health agency Rospotrebnadzor says "pneumonia of unknown etiology" and no lab accident. No plague case has been confirmed, about 200 contacts are under observation with no symptoms to date, and the WHO rates the risk "moderate to low" for Irkutsk and "very low" for Europe.

known.text: A 28-year-old laboratory technician of the Irkutsk Anti-Plague Institute was hospitalised in Shelekhov on 29 Sep with severe pneumonia and died two days later.
Rospotrebnadzor calls it "pneumonia of unknown etiology" and says her samples showed no microorganisms linked to her professional work.
Two commissions found "no evidence of an accident involving pathogenic microorganisms" at the institute; no other infectious complaints among staff in the preceding 10 days.
known.src: Rospotrebnadzor via TASS / DW fact check, 6 Oct

known.text: All close contacts are under medical observation with daily testing; the tests found 2 COVID-19 and 2 rhinovirus infections and nothing else. Nobody has shown symptoms.
known.src: Rospotrebnadzor via Moscow Times, 5 Oct · WHO via The Guardian, 6 Oct

known.text: WHO: risk "moderate to low" for Irkutsk, "low" for Russia, "very low" for Europe; no sign of a wider outbreak.
Masks became mandatory at the Irkutsk Aluminium Plant in Shelekhov on 3 Oct; several Irkutsk hospitals restricted access; Governor Kobzev says quarantined relatives may be discharged next week.
The US (Rubio: "cause for focus", Trump: "we'll help"), the European Commission ("very closely" monitoring) and Latvia's health authorities are watching the case.
known.src: Moscow Times, 5 Oct · The Guardian, 6 Oct · BNN, 6 Oct

unconfirmed.text: Whether it was plague at all. Russian media, Telegram channels and the head of Buryatia said pneumonic plague; Rospotrebnadzor says pneumonia of unknown cause.
How she fell ill. Two media accounts: a broken test tube with the plague agent around 25 Sep, or illness after a trip to Thailand. Rospotrebnadzor says there was no accident.
unconfirmed.src: Meduza, 5 Oct · DW fact check, 6 Oct

unconfirmed.text: Her name and age. Media report Darya Shipilova, 28 (El País: 27); officials have not confirmed them.
The exact date of death: Russian media say 1 Oct, WHO (via CBS) and El País say the night into 2 Oct.
The contact count (~197, Izvestia; 189 hospitalised, REN TV) comes from media; authorities say "nearly 200" tested but publish no number.
The claim that "several hundred" were infected (X post, 320,000 views) is unproven; so is the "WHO fact-sheet update was linked" claim — the update was a scheduled publication.

timeline.text: Media: she broke a test tube holding the plague agent in the lab. Rospotrebnadzor: no accident.
Admitted to the Shelekhov district hospital with severe pneumonia.
She dies of severe pneumonia. FSB officers reportedly escort ambulances taking her contacts for examination.
Russian media and Telegram report pneumonic plague. Governor Kobzev meets chief sanitary doctor Popova over "a suspected case of a particularly dangerous infection". Izvestia: 197 people quarantined.
Masks mandatory at the Irkutsk Aluminium Plant. Baikalsk urges residents not to travel to Shelekhov, then deletes the post. REN TV deletes five posts about plague.

People of Baikal: three-week quarantines at Irkutsk hospitals No. 1, 3, 10 and the children's hospital. Rospotrebnadzor: situation "stable", "pneumonia of unknown cause", no microorganisms linked to her work.
White House monitoring the reports, "assessing options" (Axios scoop).

Rospotrebnadzor: no lab accident, contacts' daily tests show 2 COVID-19 and 2 rhinovirus. Kremlin refers all questions to Rospotrebnadzor. Rubio: "not cause for alarm, but cause for focus". EU Commission monitoring "very closely".
Trump: "I hate to see them having it. We'll help."

WHO (Geneva): risk "moderate to low" for Irkutsk, "low" for Russia, "very low" for Europe; no contact symptomatic. Rubio: "incumbent upon Russia to share more information". Peskov: rely on Rospotrebnadzor, not rumours. Rospotrebnadzor offers to help the US with its own measles and plague cases.

DW fact check: lab-accident claim unproven; "hundreds infected" and "WHO fact-sheet" claims misleading; viral video is from Kabardino-Balkaria, 31 Aug. Moscow Times: Irkutsk maternity hospital screens patients. Latvia's health authorities monitoring.

context.title: What it is and what to do
context.note: This applies only if the cause turns out to be plague, which has not been confirmed.
bullets: Plague is caused by the bacterium Yersinia pestis, which lives in small wild mammals and their fleas; it is endemic in parts of Siberia.
Bubonic plague comes from flea bites and rarely spreads between people. Pneumonic plague, the lung form, spreads from person to person through respiratory droplets.
Incubation is short: typically one to three days for the pneumonic form, up to seven for bubonic.
It is treatable with common antibiotics if caught early; untreated pneumonic plague is almost always fatal. Close contacts of a pneumonic case get preventive antibiotics.
Around 2,000 cases a year occur worldwide, mostly in Africa, Asia and the Americas; a fatal case was recorded in New Mexico in June 2026.
